metric.name: frame_ui_time_p95_ms
metric.sql_used:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
WITH
  window_frames AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.upid, f.ui_thread_utid, a.id, a.dur, a.jank_type
    FROM android_frames_layers AS f
    JOIN actual_frame_timeline_slice AS a ON a.id = f.actual_frame_timeline_id
    WHERE f.layer_name NOT GLOB '*SurfaceView*' AND a.dur > 0
  ),
  app AS (
    SELECT upid FROM window_frames GROUP BY upid ORDER BY count(*) DESC, upid LIMIT 1
  ),
  frames AS (
    SELECT * FROM window_frames WHERE upid = (SELECT upid FROM app)
  ),
  ranked AS (
    SELECT s.dur AS ns, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY s.dur) AS rank,
      count(*) OVER () AS n
    FROM android_frames_choreographer_do_frame AS d
    JOIN slice AS s USING (id)
    WHERE d.ui_thread_utid IN (SELECT ui_thread_utid FROM frames)
  )
SELECT (SELECT ns / 1e6 FROM ranked WHERE rank = (n * 95 + 99) / 100) AS value

claims.text: The app UI-frame p95 increased from 32.532333 ms in the baseline to 35.181834 ms in the current trace, a 2.649501 ms worsening.

claims.text: The change is localized to com.superplayer.demo's UI thread: its average Choreographer#doFrame duration rose from 11.2807660049358 ms to 12.8092791337513 ms, while the frame count was similar.

citations.sql:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
SELECT p.name AS process_name, t.name AS thread_name, COUNT(*) AS frames, MAX(s.dur)/1e6 AS max_ms, AVG(s.dur)/1e6 AS avg_ms
FROM android_frames_choreographer_do_frame AS d
JOIN slice AS s USING (id)
JOIN thread AS t ON t.utid = d.ui_thread_utid
JOIN process AS p ON p.upid = t.upid
GROUP BY p.name, t.name
ORDER BY frames DESC;

INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
SELECT p.name AS process_name, t.name AS thread_name, COUNT(*) AS frames, MAX(s.dur)/1e6 AS max_ms, AVG(s.dur)/1e6 AS avg_ms
FROM android_frames_choreographer_do_frame AS d
JOIN slice AS s USING (id)
JOIN thread AS t ON t.utid = d.ui_thread_utid
JOIN process AS p ON p.upid = t.upid
GROUP BY p.name, t.name
ORDER BY frames DESC;

caveats: This conclusion is based on one capture per side, so run-to-run variability cannot be excluded.
The culprit attribution is correlated rather than direct: the trace localizes the regression to UI-frame work, but does not identify the Kotlin statement that caused it.
The capture ran on an Android emulator (sdk_gphone64_arm64, SDK 36).
